unit.title: How Long Has This Been Happening?

grammar_concept.title: Present Perfect Continuous
grammar_concept.rule: Use 'have/has been + verb-ing' to talk about an action that started in the past and is still continuing now (or has only just stopped), emphasizing the duration or the activity itself — not the result.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: This tense answers "how long has this been going on?". Compare: "I've painted the fence" (finished, the result matters) vs. "I've been painting the fence" (that's why my hands are dirty — the activity and its duration matter, not whether it's finished).
grammar_concept.example: I've been working here for five years. She's been studying English since she was a teenager.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Tenho trabalhado aqui há cinco anos. Ela tem estudado inglês desde que era adolescente.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: O português exprime esta mesma ideia de duração até agora com o Presente Simples e "há"/"desde" ("Trabalho aqui há cinco anos") — não existe um tempo verbal equivalente ao Present Perfect Continuous. Isso leva falantes de português a dizer "I work here for five years" em vez de "I've been working here for five years", esquecendo por completo a estrutura "have/has been + -ing".
grammar_concept.correction: Sempre que falar de uma duração que começou no passado e continua agora — normalmente com "for" (um período) ou "since" (um ponto de partida) — use "have/has been + verbo-ing", nunca o Presente Simples como se faz em português.
grammar_concept.real_world_example: In a job interview: "I've been working in customer service for three years now."

vocabulary.definition_en: used before a period of time to say how long something has lasted
example_sentences: I've been living here for two years.

vocabulary.definition_en: used before a specific point in time to say when something started
recently, in the period up to now
example_sentences: I've been feeling quite tired lately.

exercises.prompt: Complete: I ___ (wait) for the bus for twenty minutes.
exercises.explanation: Ação com duração desde o passado até agora, ligada a "for" — pede Present Perfect Continuous: "have been waiting".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar o Presente Simples ("I wait") é o erro mais comum, por transferência direta do português "espero há vinte minutos".

exercises.prompt: Complete: She ___ (work) at that company since 2020.
exercises.explanation: "Since 2020" marca um ponto de partida específico — pede Present Perfect Continuous: "has been working".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "works" (Presente Simples) em vez da forma composta é comum, sobretudo com "since".

exercises.prompt: Which word introduces a specific starting point in time, like "___ 2020"?
exercises.explanation: "Since" introduz um ponto de partida ("since 2020", "since Monday"); "for" introduz uma duração ("for two years").
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Confundir "since" com "for" é um erro muito comum.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. How long has Marta been learning English?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "I've been learning English for six years now."
exercises.transcript: I've been learning English for six years now, and I've been feeling much more confident lately, especially since I started talking to an AI tutor every day.

exercises.prompt: Read: "Tiago has been working as a nurse since 2018. Lately, he has also been studying for a management certificate at night." What has Tiago been doing lately, besides working?
exercises.explanation: O texto diz diretamente "he has also been studying for a management certificate at night".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Tenho estudado inglês há dois anos."
correct_answer: I have been studying English for two years.
I've been studying English for two years.
exercises.explanation: Duração desde o passado até agora, com "for" — pede "have been studying", não o Presente Simples.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir "tenho estudado" como "I study" ou "I have studied" (sem o "-ing") são os erros mais comuns aqui.

lesson.title: How Long Has This Been Happening?

steps.content: "Been" in this structure is usually pronounced as the weak form /bɪn/ in natural speech (not the stressed /biːn/), and "have"/"has" contract heavily: "I've been", "she's been" — almost never said in full in conversation.

steps.prompt: Talk about something you have been doing lately — learning something, working on a project, or a habit — and say how long you've been doing it.
Write 3 sentences about things you have been doing recently, using "have/has been + -ing", with at least one using "for" and one using "since".
